title: Switch activity shortcut order
line: Holding Meta and pressing A repeatedly now walks through activities in most-recently-used order, like Alt+Tab, instead of bouncing back after the first step.
explanation: The activity switcher froze its most-recently-used list (setInhibitUpdates) only when it decided to show itself, 100 ms after Meta+A. The first switch therefore happened with a live list: the new activity jumped to the top and its last-used time was saved, so the next Meta+A went back to where you started and later single switches went to the wrong activity. Now the list is frozen as soon as Meta+A is pressed, and the order and last-used times are committed only once the modifier is released (or right away for a single tap).

commits.message:
activitymanager: freeze the activity order on the first Meta+A press

The switcher only froze the most-recently-used order once it decided to
show itself, so the first switch already reordered the list and saved
its time, sending later presses back. Freeze it on the keypress instead.

BUG: 419499

media.caption: MRU order C, B, A. Holding Meta: first A goes to B, which jumps to the top; second A goes back to C.
Same steps: the list stays C, B, A and the second A reaches A.
Walk C→B→C, then a single Meta+A goes to B instead of the previous activity.
Walk C→B→A, then a single Meta+A returns to C.

reviews.text: Correctly fixes the root cause by freezing SortedActivitiesModel on the first Meta+A keypress rather than after the 100 ms switcher delay, eliminating the first-step MRU reordering and bounce-back. However, setShouldShowSwitcher(false) now calls m_runningActivitiesModel->setInhibitUpdates(false) before onCurrentActivityChanged() writes and syncs the updated LastUsed timestamps, reversing the original commit-then-unfreeze order and causing the model to unfreeze and re-sort with stale timestamps.
changes: Commit the current activity and sync LastUsed timestamps before calling m_runningActivitiesModel->setInhibitUpdates(false) in setShouldShowSwitcher(false) (e.g. via a private commit helper or a separate inhibit flag checked in onCurrentActivityChanged) so SortedActivitiesModel unfreezes only after the new timestamps are persisted.

reviews.text: Right root cause and layer: freezing SortedActivitiesModel on the keypress instead of after the 100 ms show delay fixes the walk order. But setShouldShowSwitcher(false) now calls setInhibitUpdates(false) (which re-sorts at once through setDynamicSortFilter(true)) before onCurrentActivityChanged() writes the LastUsed times, while the old code wrote the times first and then unfroze. Every switch writes the same 'now' to the old and new activity, so after a walk C->B->A the start activity C still ties with B in the stale sort and the UUID tie-break picks one; nothing re-sorts after the write, so the next single Meta+A can still go to B, which is the second half of the bug. The rig check that the single press returned to C may have passed on a lucky UUID order.
changes: Write the LastUsed times before the model re-sorts on release: e.g. track the 'walk in progress' state in SwitcherBackend (or pass a force flag to onCurrentActivityChanged) so the commit happens while the model is still frozen and setInhibitUpdates(false) comes after it, or explicitly invalidate()/sort() the model after the write.
Re-verify with two activities whose stored LastUsed times tie (the normal case after one switch), in both UUID orders, that walk C->B->A then a single Meta+A returns to C.
